Docker CLI/daemon access was broken this session: docker ps/docker compose ps failed with 'Cannot connect to the Docker daemon at unix:///var/run/docker.sock'. Diagnosed before touching anything further: /var/run/docker.pid pointed at PID 3925615, a dockerd process still alive (cwd = this workspace, still holding an open LISTEN fd on a docker.sock inode via lsof -U), but stat showed the /var/run/docker.sock *path* now resolves to a different, newer inode created by systemd's docker.socket unit, itself left in a failed (start-limit-hit) state -- i.e. the daemon owning this workspace's containers is alive and undisturbed, its API socket path was just reclaimed by a competing systemd unit. This is the same failure mode a prior TEST-RUNNER run on this host already hit and documented (test/reports/report-2026-08-26-WF02-REQ151-20260826.yaml). Did not force-kill or otherwise touch dockerd 3925615, since it also backs other unrelated running services on this shared host (penpot/immich postgres processes observed still running under it). Instead confirmed via ss -tlnp that this checkout's own Postgres container was already up (docker-proxy forwarding 0.0.0.0:5463/[::]:5463 -> 172.27.0.2:5432) and that the untracked .env sets LETFLOW_DB_PORT=5463, which config/db_port.exs resolves to for both dev and test; a /dev/tcp probe confirmed 127.0.0.1:5463 accepts connections. So docker compose up -d was unnecessary here and Ecto reached the already-running container directly; each partition's mix test alias ran ecto.create/ecto.migrate --quiet automatically per scripts/test_parallel.sh's own design.

Zero failures across all 8 partitions, so no Failure-Attribution-Is-Structural analysis was needed -- nothing to attribute, nothing to file. ISS-0340 (flaky context_test.exs) did not reproduce -- test/letflow/api/context_test.exs shows 0 failures this run.
